fetch_add.title: How fetch_add works on atomics
fetch_add.description: Adds to an atomic integer and returns the previous value, safely across threads.

slides.caption: Each fetch_add is one indivisible step: no update is ever lost.
Works for every AtomicI*/AtomicU* type. SeqCst is the safe default ordering.

load.title: How load works on atomics
load.description: Reads the current value of an atomic integer.

slides.caption: load reads the value without tearing, even while other threads write.
Relaxed ordering is enough for simple statistics; use SeqCst when unsure.

store.title: How store works on atomics
store.description: Writes a new value into an atomic integer.

slides.caption: store replaces the value in one indivisible step.
swap does the same and also returns the old value.

fetch_sub.title: How fetch_sub works on atomics
fetch_sub.description: Subtracts and returns the previous value.

slides.caption: The returned old value tells you who reached zero first.
if x.fetch_sub(1, ..) == 1 { /* I was the last one */ } is a common pattern.

swap.title: How swap works on atomics
swap.description: Stores a new value and returns the old one, in one step.

slides.caption: swap is store plus "what was there before?".
Handy to take a pending count and reset it: x.swap(0, ..).

compare_exchange.title: How compare_exchange works on atomics
compare_exchange.description: Stores a new value only if the current one is what you expect.

slides.caption: The building block of lock-free code: change it only if nobody else did in the meantime.
The value is 5 as expected: it becomes 10.
Someone changed it to 6: Err(6), nothing is written.
On Err you get the actual value, so you can retry with it.

fetch_max.title: How fetch_max works on atomics
fetch_max.description: Keeps the larger of the current and the given value.

slides.caption: Many threads can report scores; only the highest survives.

fetch_update.title: How fetch_update works on atomics
fetch_update.description: Applies a function to the value, retrying until no other thread interferes.

slides.caption: The closure returns Some(new value), or None to give up.
The old value is returned in Ok.
It loops over compare_exchange for you.

atomicbool-store.title: How AtomicBool::store works
atomicbool-store.description: Sets a flag that every thread can see.

slides.caption: A common way to tell worker threads to stop.
Workers checking load() see false and stop.

atomicbool-swap.title: How AtomicBool::swap works
atomicbool-swap.description: Sets the flag and returns what it was.

slides.caption: Exactly one thread sees false: the one that flipped the flag.
A tiny "run once" or "claim this job" mechanism.

fetch_or.title: How AtomicBool::fetch_or works
fetch_or.description: Sets the flag to (flag OR value) and returns the old flag.

slides.caption: Once any thread reports true, the flag stays true.
A later success cannot clear it.

new.title: How Atomic*::new works
new.description: Creates an atomic integer that threads can update without a lock.

slides.caption: Every AtomicI*/AtomicU* type has the same methods.
No Mutex needed for simple counters.

fetch_min.title: How fetch_min works on atomics
fetch_min.description: Keeps the smaller of the current and the given value.

slides.caption: Many threads can report times; only the lowest survives.

fetch_and.title: How fetch_and works on atomics
fetch_and.description: Bitwise AND with a value; returns the previous value.

slides.caption: fetch_or sets bits, fetch_xor toggles them.

atomic-fetch_or.title: How fetch_or works on atomics
atomic-fetch_or.description: Bitwise OR with a value; returns the previous value.

slides.caption: The returned old value tells if the bit was already set.

fetch_xor.title: How fetch_xor works on atomics
fetch_xor.description: Bitwise XOR with a value: toggles bits; returns the previous value.

slides.caption: Every bit set in the mask is flipped.
Applying the same XOR twice restores the value.

fetch_nand.title: How fetch_nand works on atomics
fetch_nand.description: Stores NOT (current AND value); returns the previous value.

slides.caption: 1100 AND 1010 = 1000; NOT of that sets every other bit.
Completes the set of atomic bit operations.

compare_exchange_weak.title: How compare_exchange_weak works on atomics
compare_exchange_weak.description: Like compare_exchange, but may fail spuriously; meant for retry loops.

title.text: a.compare_exchange_weak(cur, cur * 2, SeqCst, SeqCst)   // in a loop

l2.text: success (or retry with the new value)

slides.caption: On some CPUs the weak version is faster inside a loop.
Retry if it failed or changed.
fetch_update writes this loop for you.

get_mut.title: How get_mut works on atomics
get_mut.description: A plain &mut to the integer when you own the atomic exclusively.

slides.caption: &mut guarantees no other thread can touch it.

into_inner.title: How into_inner works on atomics
into_inner.description: Consumes the atomic and returns the plain integer.

slides.caption: After the threads are finished, take the final value.
With Arc, first get it back with Arc::into_inner.

atomicbool-new.title: How AtomicBool::new works
atomicbool-new.description: A boolean flag that threads can read and write without a lock.

slides.caption: Common as a stop signal for worker threads.
const, so it works in statics.

atomicbool-compare_exchange.title: How AtomicBool::compare_exchange works
atomicbool-compare_exchange.description: Sets the flag only if it currently has the expected value.

slides.caption: Exactly one thread wins the claim.

atomicbool-fetch_and.title: How AtomicBool::fetch_and works
atomicbool-fetch_and.description: Sets the flag to (flag AND value); returns the old flag.

slides.caption: Once any thread reports false, it stays false.

atomicbool-fetch_xor.title: How AtomicBool::fetch_xor works
atomicbool-fetch_xor.description: Toggles the flag if the value is true; returns the old flag.

slides.caption: XOR with true flips the flag.

fetch_not.title: How AtomicBool::fetch_not works
fetch_not.description: Flips the flag; returns the old value.

slides.caption: The old value true is returned.

atomicbool-fetch_nand.title: How AtomicBool::fetch_nand works
atomicbool-fetch_nand.description: Sets the flag to NOT (flag AND value).

slides.caption: true AND true = true; NOT gives false.

atomicbool-get_mut.title: How AtomicBool::get_mut works
atomicbool-get_mut.description: A plain &mut bool when you own the flag exclusively.

slides.caption: Exclusive access makes atomic operations unnecessary.

atomicbool-into_inner.title: How AtomicBool::into_inner works
atomicbool-into_inner.description: Consumes the atomic and returns the plain bool.

slides.caption: Take the final value once threads are finished.

atomicptr-new.title: How AtomicPtr::new works
atomicptr-new.description: A raw pointer that threads can swap atomically.

slides.caption: A building block for lock-free data structures.
Reading through the pointer needs unsafe.
The pointer value itself is read atomically.

atomicptr-compare_exchange.title: How AtomicPtr::compare_exchange works
atomicptr-compare_exchange.description: Swaps the pointer only if it still points where you expect.

a0t.text: points at a, swap to b

slides.caption: How lock-free stacks push and pop.
It points at a, as expected.

atomicptr-get_mut.title: How AtomicPtr::get_mut works
atomicptr-get_mut.description: A plain &mut to the pointer when you own the AtomicPtr exclusively.

slides.caption: Exclusive access, so a normal write is fine.

fence.title: How atomic::fence works
fence.description: A memory barrier: orders memory operations around it across threads.

l1.text: fence(Release): earlier writes cannot move after this

slides.caption: Fences let several relaxed operations share one ordering guarantee.
An acquire fence on the reader pairs with it.
When unsure, SeqCst operations without fences are simpler.

compiler_fence.title: How atomic::compiler_fence works
compiler_fence.description: Stops the compiler (not the CPU) from reordering memory operations across it.

slides.caption: Only for code interrupted on the same thread, like signal handlers.
...stay before it in the compiled code.
Between threads, use fence or atomic orderings instead.

update.title: How update works on atomics
update.description: Applies a function to the value atomically, retrying as needed; returns the old value.

slides.caption: The closure may run several times if other threads interfere.
try_update lets the closure give up.

try_update.title: How try_update works on atomics
try_update.description: Applies a function that may refuse (None); Ok(old) or Err(current).

slides.caption: Returning None leaves the value unchanged.
Same as fetch_update with clearer naming.

as_ptr.title: How as_ptr works on atomics
as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the underlying integer, for FFI.

slides.caption: Accessing it non-atomically while others use the atomic is a data race.
Read through it (no other threads here).
Pass it to C code expecting an atomic int.

from_ptr.title: How from_ptr works on atomics
from_ptr.description: Treats a raw pointer to an integer as an atomic (unsafe).

slides.caption: The memory must be aligned and only used atomically meanwhile.
Common with memory shared by C code.

from_mut.title: How from_mut works on atomics
from_mut.description: Treats a &mut integer as an atomic.

slides.caption: Safe: &mut proves nobody else is using it.
Then lend & of it to scoped threads.

atomicbool-update.title: How AtomicBool::update works
atomicbool-update.description: Applies a function to the flag atomically; returns the old value.

atomicbool-try_update.title: How AtomicBool::try_update works
atomicbool-try_update.description: Applies a function that may refuse; Ok(old) or Err(current).

atomicbool-compare_exchange_weak.title: How AtomicBool::compare_exchange_weak works
atomicbool-compare_exchange_weak.description: Like compare_exchange, but may fail spuriously; use in a loop.

slides.caption: Can be faster on some CPUs.

atomicbool-as_ptr.title: How AtomicBool::as_ptr works
atomicbool-as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the underlying bool.

slides.caption: Non-atomic access while shared is a data race.

atomicbool-from_ptr.title: How AtomicBool::from_ptr works
atomicbool-from_ptr.description: Treats a raw pointer to a bool as an AtomicBool (unsafe).

slides.caption: Must only be used atomically meanwhile.

atomicbool-from_mut.title: How AtomicBool::from_mut works
atomicbool-from_mut.description: Treats a &mut bool as an AtomicBool.

slides.caption: Lend & of it to scoped threads.

fetch_ptr_add.title: How AtomicPtr::fetch_ptr_add works
fetch_ptr_add.description: Moves the stored pointer forward by n elements; returns the old pointer.

slides.caption: Like an atomic cursor through a buffer.

fetch_ptr_sub.title: How AtomicPtr::fetch_ptr_sub works
fetch_ptr_sub.description: Moves the stored pointer back by n elements; returns the old pointer.

fetch_byte_add.title: How AtomicPtr::fetch_byte_add works
fetch_byte_add.description: Moves the stored pointer forward by n bytes; returns the old pointer.

slides.caption: Keep the result aligned before reading.

fetch_byte_sub.title: How AtomicPtr::fetch_byte_sub works
fetch_byte_sub.description: Moves the stored pointer back by n bytes; returns the old pointer.

atomicptr-compare_exchange_weak.title: How AtomicPtr::compare_exchange_weak works
atomicptr-compare_exchange_weak.description: Swaps the pointer if it is the expected one; may fail spuriously.

atomicptr-update.title: How AtomicPtr::update works
atomicptr-update.description: Applies a function to the stored pointer atomically; returns the old one.

atomicptr-try_update.title: How AtomicPtr::try_update works
atomicptr-try_update.description: Applies a function that may refuse; Ok(old) or Err(current).

slides.caption: Returning None leaves it as is.

atomicptr-as_ptr.title: How AtomicPtr::as_ptr works
atomicptr-as_ptr.description: A raw pointer to the stored pointer.

atomicptr-from_ptr.title: How AtomicPtr::from_ptr works
atomicptr-from_ptr.description: Treats a raw pointer-to-pointer as an AtomicPtr (unsafe).

slides.caption: Must be aligned and accessed only atomically meanwhile.

atomicptr-from_mut.title: How AtomicPtr::from_mut works
atomicptr-from_mut.description: Treats a &mut *mut T as an AtomicPtr.
